description: Collection mapping: six lens inventories of winning unit files, each with an adversarial verification (corrections, missed assets). Generated on 2026-10-06/07 against the repo at 50cad91b. Unit ids were resolved through integration/missions/refine_civ_traffic.py winning_file(); apply each lens verify.corrections before use.

inventory.lens: United States Navy, US Marine Corps and Military Sealift Command. All three declare Nation=US. The files have no separate MSC or USMC nation key; MSC hulls are recognisable only by display text such as 'USNS' or a 'T-' hull prefix.

mappings.notes: Nation=US. Hull variants: the 2025 unit covers CVN-68 to CVN-75 (NumberOfVariants=8, so no CVN-76 or CVN-77). The 2027s_adou unit covers CVN-68 to 73, 75 and 77; it declares 10 variants but Variant7 and Variant9 are absent. usn_cvn_nimitz has CVN-68 to 77 but a 1980s air wing (F-14A, A-6E, S-3A, SH-3H). AirGroup check failed on both modern units: usn_fa-18e Squadron3 to Squadron42 do not exist, because the winning squadron file is 3430135740 and it defines only VFA-115 and VFA-143. usn_ea-18g Squadron8 to 17 do not exist. usn_fa-18f Squadron3 to 9 belong to Ace Combat fictional nations (ISAF, Erusea, Belkan, Osea). The 2027 variants embark usn_mh-60r_26, which does not resolve. Set the wing per placement with a mission-level CustomAirGroup. FlightDeck capacity 85 aircraft, 1.2M ammo points (Phoenix, Harpoon, AirTorpedo, AdvancedARM; the 2027 unit adds Bomb). No [SupplySystem].

Nation=US. Variants: CVN-78 to 81 for the Ford mod units, CVN-78 to 83 for the RSA unit. The usn_cvn_ford_jsf base AirGroup is the only modern carrier wing that passes the check: F/A-18E (VFA-115/143) x24, F/A-18F Sq1 x12, F-35C Sq1 (VX-9 livery) x24, EA-18G x6, E-2D VAW-121 x4, MH-60R HSM-35 x10. However, all four of its hull variants replace the helicopters with the unresolved usn_mh-60r_26, and it has no FlightDeck_AmmoCapacity key. usn_cvn_ford's base wing uses F/A-18F Squadron9 (Nation=Osea). usn_cvn_gerald_r_ford's variants use RSA Hornets with real VFA liveries but SH-3J Sea Kings as the helicopters; its Variant2 references E-2D Squadron10, which does not exist. usn_cvn_ford_legacy (empty deck) also resolves.

usn_fa_18e_rsa has 17 USN squadrons (VFA-14, 27, 31, 37, 83, 86, 87, 94, 97, 105, 115, 136, 137, 143, 151, 192, 195) plus VX-4. usn_fa-18e's winning squadron file declares 20 squadrons but defines only Squadron1 (VFA-115) and Squadron2 (VFA-143); USNA's 49-squadron file (3737267013) is outranked. The fleet's home stations at Lemoore and Oceana are not in the node list.

blk3: VFA-2, 11, 22, 32, 41, 94, 102 (Sq8 is RAAF). rsa: VFA-2, 11, 22, 41, 97, 102, 103, 106 (FRS), 122 (FRS), 154, 213. usn_fa-18f: Sq1 VFA-187 (uses texture vfa-122.png) and Sq2 VFA-103 are US; Sq3 to 9 are Ace Combat nations, so do not use them for USN.

mappings.role_family: Carrier air wing / shore: electronic attack
mappings.notes: usn_ea-18g_2020 has 19 US VAQ squadrons (VAQ-129 FRS through 144, plus VAQ-209), which is the best fit for a Growler home station. usn_ea-18g has VAQ-131, 132, 133, 138 plus RAAF 6 SQN. rsa has 6 VAQ squadrons.
SEST squadrons: VFA-147, 97, 86, 115, 125 (FRS), 101, VMFA-314 and VMFA-311 (USMC F-35C), and VX-9. RSA adds VMFA-58.
Squadrons VAW-112, 114, 116, 117, 121, 122, 123, 124, 125. Defined squadrons stop at Squadron9. For E-2C, usn_e_2c_group2_plus (RSA) resolves.

19 US squadrons (HSM-35 to HSM-79) plus 816 Sqn RAN. It is embarked by the 3390330875 and 3606774881 cruisers and destroyers (x2), Freedom LCS (x1) and Zumwalt. RSA-derived hulls embark SH-2G instead. Model and FLIR depend on 3590477166 (see docs/collection-interop-audit.md).
The Seahawk airframe exists but there is no MH-60S unit and no HSC squadron. HH-60H (HS-1 to HS-15 liveries) is the closest stand-in and needs an 'MH-60S stand-in' label.
V-22 airframes exist only with USMC VMM/VMMT liveries; there is no Navy VRM livery and no CMV-22B variant. No carrier AirGroup embarks a V-22. C-2A Greyhound: none.
No MQ-25. There is no carrier-borne tanker of any kind: no F/A-18 carries a RefuelSystem. usn_fury_* (3804868806, Anduril FQ-44) are combat wingmen, not tankers.

The 2025 unit carries CG-62 Robert Smalls, CG-64, CG-65 and CG-71 with MH-60R x2. The 2027 unit carries CG-64, 65 and 71. The 2018 unit has 15 hulls (CG-52 to 73). ticonderogaVLS has 27 hulls but embarks SH-2G. No supply system on any of them.

Hull-group variants: 051 is DDG-51; 052 is DDG-52, 53, 55, 57; 054 is DDG-54, 56, 58-61, 63, 65-70; 064 is DDG-64 and 71. usn_ddg_burke_f1_062_late (DDG-62, NSM) also resolves. No AirGroup, which is correct for Flight I. Single-unit alternative: usn_ddg_arleigh_burke_flight1_2025 (SEST over RSA, 21 hulls).
072 covers DDG-72, 73, 74, 76, 77; 075 covers DDG-75 and 78. No hangar.

Per-hull-group units _079_late, _080_late, _081_late, _084_late, _085_late, _089_late, _091_late, _097_late, _100_late, _108_late (3390330875) and _117 also resolve and together cover DDG-79 to 112 with real names. Air group is MH-60R x2 plus SH-60B. Single-unit alternative: usn_ddg_arleigh_burke_flight2a_2026 (SEST over RSA, 47 hulls), which embarks SH-2G.
usn_ddg_burke_f3_125 has 25 hull variants (DDG-125 onward) with MH-60R x2. The 2030 SEST/RSA unit embarks SH-2G.
Variants are DDG-1000 and 1001; the CPS unit adds DDG-1002. MH-60R x2.
Early covers LCS-1 to 15 (odd numbers); late covers LCS-17 to 31. SUW package only, no MCM or ASW module. MH-60R x1.
No trimaran hull in the collection. Label as 'Independence-class stand-in'. The mine-countermeasures function is not modelled.
Variants FFG-62 to 69. Helicopters are SH-2G plus QH-50E, not MH-60R. Not yet in fleet service, so placing it is a future-dated design choice.
The only US mine warfare hulls are Cold War vanilla units (Aggressive MSO; usn_msc_adjutant also resolves). Label as a stand-in if used.

Variants LHD-1 to 8. The AirGroup check passes: F-35B VMFA-211 x6, MV-22B VMM-161 x12, AH-1Z x4, UH-1Y x3. The early unit carries AV-8B+, CH-46E and CH-46D. FlightDeck ammo 45k (Harpoon, AdvancedARM). No supply system.

usn_lha_tripoli is a fictional RSA class. Its variants are named 'Tripoli LHA-6', 'Essex LHA-7', 'America LHA-8' and so on, which does not match real hull numbers. Its air wing is AV-8B+ x10, AH-1W, CH-46 and SH-3J, with no F-35B or MV-22. Label as a stand-in and override the air group with a mission CustomAirGroup.

Squadrons VMGR-152, 153, 252 and 352 (the KC-130T adds 452). Has a RefuelSystem that passes fuel to Aircraft and Helicopter targets.

usn_ssn_seawolf_rsa, usn_ssn_seawolf_carter_rsa (3413868677) and the fictional usn_ssn_seawolf_late_rsa ('Hollywood-class') also resolve.
Variants SSGN-726 to 729.
Ohio covers SSBN-730 to 743; Columbia covers SSBN-826 to 828 and is future. Use for broad strategic presence only, in line with the plan's restraint on nuclear detail.

mappings.lookup_term: Emory S. Land / Frank Cable AS
mappings.notes: No US tender exists. The Kilauea AE serves Vessel and Submarine targets with no MaxAmmoPoints cap, so it can pass Mk48 (4695 pts) and Tomahawk (4350 pts). Label it 'AS tender stand-in'. The only real submarine tender, wp_pb_don, declares Nation=Soviet/Indonesia and so cannot represent a US ship. US_Los_Alamos (AFDB-7 floating dry dock, 3600788156) can serve as static repair scenery.

mappings.lookup_term: Henry J. Kaiser T-AO (John Lewis T-AO-205)
mappings.notes: usn_tao_kaiser is a named Kaiser unit (T-AO 187, 189, 193, 204) built on the Spanish Teide mesh (117.5 m against the real 206 m); its display name already says '(stand-in)'. Supply limit is 2000 points, so Harpoon and SM-2 pass but Tomahawk does not. The John Lewis class does not exist. civ_ms_sealift_pacific (Sealift Pacific T-AOT-168 and others; Nation=US; Role=Merchant) is an MSC tanker stand-in that carries AirTorpedo only.
Named T-AKE 1, 2, 6 and 11, built on the Kilauea mesh (172 m against the real 210 m). Supply pool 550k with no cap.
usn_taoe_supply covers T-AOE 6, 7, 8 and 10 on the Sacramento mesh, with a 700k uncapped pool and the largest stock in the collection. usn_aoe_sacramento (AOE-1 to 4) is a retired USN-crewed AOE.

Algol covers T-AKR-287 to 294 (288 m) with a 500k uncapped supply pool, but Role=Transport and it transfers only at 8 kn. There are no LMSR units. civ_ms_roro_c has RRF 'Cape' variants (Cape Isabel AKR-5062, Cape Hudson, and others) but no supply system; label it as an LMSR or RRF stand-in.

mappings.lookup_term: MPS T-AK container/RoRo; ESB Lewis B. Puller; ESD Montford Point
mappings.notes: Nation=US variants carry RRF and MSC names (Cape Fear T-AK-5061, Cape Ducato T-AKR-5051, Cape May, Cape Mohican, Cape Mendocino), but Role=Merchant and the ship classes are dated. civ_ms_c8 and civ_ms_seabee supply 300k with an 8000-point cap; roro_a supplies 80k with a 2000-point cap. ESB and ESD: none.

Squadrons VQ-1 and VQ-2. The type is retired in the real world; optional.

No military trainer exists. A Nation=US civil light single (Role=Airliner, Default squadron only) is the only stand-in and needs a visible 'T-6B stand-in' label. Use for non-combat background traffic only.
fr_as-350 Squadron2 is a plain Nation=US livery and is preferred. civ_as-350's US squadrons are civilian liveries (LAPD, Reach Air and similar). Label as 'TH-73 stand-in'.

mappings.lookup_term: NAWCAD test squadrons (VX-23, VX-20, HX-21, VX-1, UX-24)
mappings.notes: The airframes exist but no Patuxent test liveries do. The nearest are F-35C VX-9 'Vampires' (usn_f-35c Squadron1/2) and F/A-18E VX-4 'Evaluators' (usn_fa_18e_rsa Squadron18). Everything else would use fleet liveries labelled 'test det'. There are no test-instrumented loadouts.
Optional. Nation=US. This is a commercial design, not a confirmed USN program of record, so label it if used. Six armed and decoy sub-variants also resolve.
There is no Aegis Ashore or land SM-3 unit; SM-3 exists only as ship ammunition. Army Patriot and THAAD units resolve but are a different operator and system.

installations.node: San Diego / North Island (NAS North Island, NB San Diego, Point Loma, Coronado)
installations.notes: There is no named NAS unit. airbase_us is the donor that SEST RAAF Bases cloned. Its stock AirGroup is USAF-heavy and has defects: usn_fa-18f Squadron3 is Nation=ISAF, usmc_vh-3d Squadron1 is missing, and 'S-70B-2_Seahawk=Squadron1=5' is malformed. Clone and rename it the way raaf-bases did. There is no US Pacific naval port unit at all, so the surface base is 'none'.

placement_and_engine.finding: Operator is set by Nation= in the winning *_variants.ini ([Default] and [VariantN]) for ships and land units, and in *_squadrons.ini ([Default] and [SquadronN]) for aircraft. USN, USMC and MSC all use Nation=US.
placement_and_engine.evidence: mods-source/_vanilla/original/nations_reference.ini maps both the usn and usaf prefixes to NationName=US, and no MSC or USMC key exists. Per-squadron nations vary inside one aircraft: usn_fa-18f Squadron3-9 are ISAF, Erusea, Belkan and Osea; usn_p8 Squadron2-7 are allied air forces.

placement_and_engine.finding: A mission can override a ship's air group per unit, which is the practical fix for the broken Nimitz 2025/2027 and Ford variant wings.
placement_and_engine.evidence: integration/missions/DARWIN US SUPPLY.ini, [Taskforce1Vessel1] Type=usn_cvn_nimitz_2027s_adou, lines 62-68: CustomAirGroup=True followed by aircraft=Squadron,count lines. That same block names usn_mh-60r_2027, which does not resolve, so every override needs the same id check.

placement_and_engine.finding: usn_mh-60r_26, usn_fa-18e_late and usn_mh-60r_2027 do not resolve. The first two are embedded in variant air groups of usn_cvn_ford, usn_cvn_ford_jsf and usn_cvn_nimitz_2027s_adou.
placement_and_engine.evidence: find_unit_file('aircraft', id) returns None. docs/mod-catalog.md records that usn_mh-60r_26 left the 3390330875 export in the 27 Sep / 2 Oct 2026 exports.

placement_and_engine.finding: usn_fa-18e's unit is won by SEST_Integration, but its squadrons file is won by 3430135740, which defines only VFA-115 and VFA-143. Every modern carrier wing that references a higher squadron number points at nothing.
placement_and_engine.evidence: file_stack('aircraft/usn_fa-18e_squadrons.ini') returns [3430135740, 3737267013]; the first declares NumberOfSquadrons=20 and defines 2, while the second defines 49 but is outranked. docs/collection-interop-audit.md already lists this mismatch.

placement_and_engine.finding: Named US NAS and naval-station units would follow the raaf-bases pattern: clone airbase_us (vanilla Reykjavik scenery plus proven deck geometry) and set a custom AirGroup and Nation=US. A US Pacific port would need a renamed clone of a port_eastcoast_* unit. Both are new SEST units, so this is a design proposal.
placement_and_engine.evidence: integration/raaf-bases/README.md: 'Each base clones the Modern US Airbase unit'. SEST_Integration/land_units/airbase_raaf_*.ini.

placement_and_engine.finding: Ship supply covers ammunition only (TruckSupplySystem). There is no ship-to-ship fuel. Transfer is gated by category lists, MaxAmmoPoints and speed. Only the SEST-patched US auxiliaries pass categorised rounds; the RE-power freighters pass uncategorised rounds only.
placement_and_engine.evidence: integration/replenishment/README.md, supplier table and 'category gate' / 'launcher gate' sections, plus the [SupplySystem1] blocks quoted in support_and_traffic.

placement_and_engine.topic: Existing mission anchors near the US nodes
placement_and_engine.finding: No mission is centred within 300 nm of San Diego, Kitsap, Pearl Harbor, Yokosuka, Jacksonville, Whiting Field or (closer than 281 nm) Patuxent River. Anchors exist near Bahrain (75 nm), Rota (44 nm), Sigonella (49 nm), Djibouti (97 nm), Souda Bay (132 nm), Diego Garcia (184 nm), Norfolk (209 nm, Saronic Corsair test missions) and Guam (254 nm).

gaps: Carrier aviation: no MQ-25, C-2A, MH-60S/HSC or CMV-22B (Navy VRM) units. No carrier-capable tanker of any type.
USN Patuxent River test squadrons (VX-23, VX-20, HX-21, VX-1, UX-24): no liveries. Only VX-9 (F-35C) and VX-4 (RSA F/A-18E) exist.
Naval Air Training Command: no T-6B, TH-73A, TH-57 or T-45 units. The only stand-ins are a civil light single and the AS350.

inventory.method_notes:
Everything was read-only. Helper scripts are in the session scratchpad; nothing in the repo was written.

**Resolution.** I imported winning_file, find_unit_file and file_stack from integration/missions/refine_civ_traffic.py via sys.path. The only SEST token in data/load-order.tokens.txt is SEST_Integration (integration/dist/SEST_Integration), which consolidates the individual packs.

**Unit scan.**
- I listed every *.ini under vessels/, submarines/, aircraft/ and land_units/ across all load-order sources, SEST_Integration and vanilla, excluding _variants, _squadrons and _loadouts files.
- Each path was resolved with winning_file. 2,131 resolved to a unit with a UnitType. No submarines/ folder exists anywhere; submarines live in vessels/ with UnitType=Submarine.
- Anchor Chain '#!alias' and '#!extend' heads were followed through file_stack, concatenating the base and the patch, so AirGroup and SupplySystem reflect the effective file.

**Operator and names.**
- Operator is the Nation= value in the winning *_variants.ini or *_squadrons.ini.
- Display names come from language_en/{vessel_names,aircraft_names,land_units_names}.ini, merged key by key in priority order. Some high-priority mods ship empty sections, such as 3406985435 for civ_ms_sealift_pacific.

**Air groups.** Each AirGroup and each variant CustomAirGroup was validated. Every aircraft id was checked with find_unit_file, and every squadron was checked against the winning squadrons file and its Nation.

**Supply.** Supply capability is the [SupplySystemN] blocks of the winning file.

**Final check.** All 133 unit ids reported above were re-checked with find_unit_file immediately before reporting.

**Mod titles.** Taken from data/mod-catalog.json:
- 3390330875 Modern US Navy
- 3606774881 U.S. Navy 2027 Capabilities
- 3413868677 Red Storm Arsenal
- 3737267013 United States Naval Aviation
- 3433957933 Virginia/Seawolf/Ohio submarines
- 3373960386 Flight Deck Ops
- 3461044389 Gerald R. Ford CVN
- 3430135740 F/A-18 Murder Hornet
- 3592460366 Modern US Airbase
- 3605013271 RE-power

**Node associations are not from the research.** The R01-R03 reports were not available. The nodes listed for each mapping are general public-knowledge homeport and deployment context, used only as lookup hints; entries marked 'verify' especially should not be read as report content. Resident assignments, quantities and coordinates are not asserted.

**Outcome labelling.** SEST stand-in auxiliaries (T-AO, T-AKE, T-AOE) are marked 'exact' because they are named, Nation=US units of that class whose display names already carry '(stand-in)'. Their meshes are donor hulls.

verify.verdict:
The inventory is mostly sound, but several outcomes need fixing. I re-resolved all 103 distinct unit IDs in mappings, installations and support_and_traffic with find_unit_file and winning_file, plus about 35 more IDs named in the notes. Every one resolves. Every winning source, including the 'SEST over X' claims, matches file_stack. Nation=US holds throughout. The three IDs it calls unresolved (usn_mh-60r_26, usn_mh-60r_2027, usn_fa-18e_late) really are unresolved. The supply-system figures, carrier air-group failures, hull lists, mission-anchor distances and the Iceland-flagged Gulf ports all check out.

Material errors:
1. The AH-1Z mapping is an AH-1W (late) unit. The 'AH-1Z Viper' name comes from a commented-out section header in 3737267013's names file, so the outcome should be proxy, and the Wasp wing entry is wrong for the same reason.
2. 'No carrier tanker exists' is false. The vanilla KA-3B and EKA-3B carry a RefuelSystem and fly from 3373960386 carriers, so MQ-25 should be proxy rather than none, and the KC-130 'only refuellers' claim is wrong.
3. The Norfolk, Mayport and Jacksonville ports are hidden from the Mission Editor. They are campaign-layer ports that no mission places.
4. The SEST T-AO, T-AKE and T-AOE units call themselves '(stand-in)' and sit on donor meshes, so they should be proxy, not exact.
5. usa_airbase Variant1 'Naval Air Station' is a better NAS proxy and was missed.
6. The E-2D, F/A-18F Block III and SEST EA-18G squadrons show a different squadron's livery than the one named, which is visible in the .ini files.
7. Missed assets: the USMC legacy Hornets (VMFA, F/A-18C/D), the DDG-88 HELIOS hulls, the full 2027 Burke hull-group set and a 2000s Nimitz whose shipped wing actually works.

The remaining corrections are smaller precision fixes: foreign squadrons on the RSA P-8A and AV-8B+, the Belgian-only Adjutant, out-of-date ServiceDates on the Algol, Kilauea and Los Alamos units, a zero-count SH-60B entry on Flight IIA, and some squadron and hull lists. No files in the repo were modified.

Also Aegis Ashore (Deveselu, Redzikowo), Patriot/THAAD, coastal and long-range fires (NMESIS, Typhon), radars, and how the Army/DLA depots (Susquehanna, Richmond, Anniston, Red River, Tobyhanna, San Joaquin, Germersheim) could be represented.

inventory.method_notes: Read-only. The repo was not modified. Helper scripts and output are in (agent scratch, not kept) usaf_lens/ (index_units.py, index_units_lib.py, sq.py, grep_land.py, units_usaf.json). That scratchpad is shared with other subagents, and its top-level units.json was overwritten by one of them, so only use the usaf_lens/ copies. Resolution used integration/missions/refine_civ_traffic.py (winning_file, find_unit_file, file_stack) imported via sys.path. Only SEST_Integration is in data/load-order.tokens.txt, so SEST content resolves from integration/dist/SEST_Integration. I enumerated every aircraft, land_units, vessels and submarines id across vanilla, all mods-source/<id> folders and all SEST packs, then resolved each id's winning file. Nations come from the winning _squadrons.ini (aircraft) or _variants.ini (land units) Nation= keys. Display names were merged key by key down file_stack('language_en/<file>_names.ini'), matching the game's language merge. Every id reported was re-checked through find_unit_file, and ammunition through winning_file. Mod titles come from data/mod-catalog.json (keyed by workshop_id). Placement precedents come from vanilla and repo missions (NameOverride, Nation, CustomAirGroup). The R01-R03 reports were not available. The node associations in the mappings are candidate platform-to-node fits for this lens, not claims about what the reports say; the plan requires verifying resident and rotational assignments against the reports.

corrections.problem: The row says it fires usa_prsm as an anti-ship weapon. The winning 3413868677:ammunition/usa_prsm.ini has CanNotAttackTypes=Vessel,Submarine, LandAttackCapability=All and SeekerActiveRange=0, and its language entry calls it 'Land Attack'. It cannot engage ships. Only the 270 nm MaxLaunchRange and AmmoPoints=4350 are right.
corrections.fix: Describe the M270A2 as land attack only (it cannot target vessels). Keep the outcome 'exact' for US Army M270A2 with PrSM Increment 1. Do not count it as coastal anti-ship fires, and do not use it as an anti-ship HIMARS stand-in.

corrections.problem: In the 'Aegis Ashore site (visible marker only, no interceptor)' proxy row, wp_an_tpy_2 is not a passive marker. Its winning radar (3683253079 systems/sensors.ini [AN/TPY-2]) is an air-search radar with MaxRange=3000 km and HasDataLink=True that feeds the whole task force above 6,000 m. Placing it at Deveselu or Redzikowo would add a long-range BMD air picture that the real sites (which carry SPY-1) do not provide in this form. That breaks the same no-invented-deployment rule the row applies to THAAD.
corrections.fix: Remove wp_an_tpy_2 from the Aegis Ashore marker row. For a passive marker, use nato_large_ewr_station (vanilla, Visual 'Eyes' sensor only, Role=Target) or us_cobra_dane_ewr (vanilla, Nation=US, also visual only, Role=Target), each with a NameOverride. If no marker is wanted, keep the node abstract.

corrections.problem: Refuelling is reported as working through [SupplySystem1] RefuelSystem. None of the four modded tankers (usaf_stratotanker 3722749887, usaf_kc-46a_boom, usaf_kc-46a_warp 3744475027, usaf_kc-10a_extender 3740293822) has the 0.8-era [AerialRefueling] TankerSystems= block or a FuelCapacity. The vanilla usaf_kc-10 has both (TankerSystems=Boom,ProbeAndDrogue, FuelCapacity=160000), and so does usmc_kc-130j (TankerSystems=ProbeAndDrogue, FuelCapacity=25855). The repo's own docs/mod-catalog.md treats a missing [AerialRefueling] block as 'cannot tank' (F-15J row). Several US receivers in this inventory also have no ReceiverSystems: dts_b-52h, usaf_b-2_spirit, usaf_f-15e_SE, usaf_f-16cm-bl52d, usaf_e-3g, boeing-rc135. Only usaf_b-1b_dts, usaf_f-22_s6 and usaf_f-15ex_SEII declare Boom.
corrections.fix: Downgrade the aerial-refuelling engine finding and the support rows for these tankers to 'unverified in game'. Note that vanilla usaf_kc-10 is the only US boom-and-drogue tanker with the current block, and that the KC-130J serves only ProbeAndDrogue receivers (usn_f-35c, usmc_f-35b). Test a modded tanker with a Boom receiver in the editor before relying on it.

corrections.problem: The support row says it refuels 'with drogue pods for Navy and USMC receivers'. Neither KC-46 file declares TankerSystems, so receiver compatibility is not modelled. The boom file also carries refuel_drogue_L/R submodels and a [Refuelling_Pod] section. Diffing the two files shows the only functional difference: WARP has SupplySystem_MaxTargets=3 (3 stations) against 1 on the boom version, plus hose visuals.
corrections.fix: Describe the WARP version as 'refuels up to 3 aircraft at once (hose visuals)'. Do not claim probe-and-drogue compatibility.

corrections.problem: The gap list says 'Army watercraft and Army prepositioned-stock ships: none. The only US sealift unit is usn_takr_algol'. verify.verdict:
The ID resolution is clean, but several claims about function are wrong or unverified. I re-resolved 78 unit IDs through find_unit_file: every ID in mappings, installations and support_and_traffic, plus the IDs mentioned in notes. All of them exist as winning files at the claimed source (Workshop id or SEST_Integration). Declared nations, display names, squadron lists and ServiceDates match what the inventory reports. The outcome labels are mostly honest.

Corrections, most important first:
- **PrSM** (usa_mlrs_m270a2) is land attack only and cannot target vessels; the inventory calls it anti-ship.
- **AN/TPY-2** (wp_an_tpy_2) is a 3000 km datalinked air-search radar, not a passive Aegis Ashore marker. Use nato_large_ewr_station or us_cobra_dane_ewr instead.
- **Modded tankers** (KC-135, KC-46, KC-10A) lack the [AerialRefueling] TankerSystems block that vanilla usaf_kc-10 and usmc_kc-130j carry. Many US receivers also lack ReceiverSystems, so in-game refuelling is unverified. The KC-46 WARP difference is MaxTargets=3, not drogue compatibility.
- **Sealift gap is wrong**: Nation=US Ready Reserve Force ro-ros exist (civ_ms_roro_c and civ_ms_roro_a Cape-class variants), so usn_takr_algol is not the only US sealift.
- **Placement precedents**: Sigonella, Souda and Andersen project to points about 23, 15 and 7.5 nm from the real fields. Only Diego Garcia and Tindal are within about 1 nm.
- **F-15EX nuclear loadout**: Strike183N (W62 AGM-183) is not flagged.
- **Patriot resupply**: Patriot rounds are unpriced, so HEMTT and M923 can reload them, contrary to the 'light rounds only' note.
- **Smaller fixes**: rok_uh60 is an ASW-only Korean airframe; the MV-75 date wording is misleading; usa_tempest_launcher is fictional; the depot note contradicts nv_headquarters; airbase_us at Camp Lemonnier needs a NameOverride; the E-7A row's arrays are misaligned.

Missed assets include A-10C, UH-1Y and CH-46E as stand-ins, the larger airfield_us_large for Andersen, SL-AMRAAM, Patriot GEM-T, Cobra Dane and the RRF ro-ros.

inventory.method_notes: Read-only. Scratch scripts are under (agent scratch, not kept) (index.py, nations.py, nm.py, dump.py, sq.py). I imported winning_file, find_unit_file and file_stack from integration/missions/refine_civ_traffic.py. I enumerated every vessels/, aircraft/ and land_units/ id across vanilla, all mods-source/<id>/ and integration/*/SEST_* (2,133 unit ids), resolved each through the canonical load order, and filtered on Nation= values from the winning _variants/_squadrons files (289 China-bearing units) plus pla/plan/plaaf/china prefixes. Only SEST_Integration is in data/load-order.tokens.txt, so SEST content is reported from integration/dist/SEST_Integration with the originating pack noted. Display names were rebuilt by merging language_en sections key by key in load order, following name-fixes/build_patch.py. All 116 unit IDs cited were re-checked to resolve. AirGroup lines were validated against the winning aircraft and squadron files. Supply roles come from [SupplySystemN] blocks. Mod titles and positions come from data/mod-catalog.json and the load order. Meshes were read from ResourcesRoot/AssetBundleMesh to separate custom models from kitbashes. Absence claims (075, 076, 815, 904, hospital ship, KJ-200, H-6G, UAVs, Djibouti) rest on greps of all winning unit IDs, merged names and raw vessel and name files. Node associations in 'nodes' are candidate relevance from the plan's region table and general platform role. No resident assignment is asserted, and the R01-R03 research files on the draft branch were deliberately not read, per the task. Runtime behaviour (spawning with dangling AirGroup refs, inland placement, Nation=china override on RE-power docks, supply transfer) is inferred from files and in-repo or vanilla mission precedent, not tested in game.

verify.verdict:
The inventory holds up well overall. All 93 unit IDs I checked from mappings, installations and support_and_traffic resolve through winning_file/find_unit_file to the stated winning sources, and their nation and role are as stated. Most outcome labels are honest. Absence claims checked by grep (075, 076, 815, 904, hospital ship, KJ-200, H-6G, Djibouti, CCG) hold. The AirGroup defects on the Liaoning and on pla_airbase_modern are confirmed.

Errors to fix:
- One factual error: plan_cv_fujian_rsa's variants carry a resolving RSA air wing; it is not empty.
- One stale recommendation: Liaoning Variant2 is in date only for 2022-2023.
- One label-honesty problem: the Type 035 row puts the Song and Kilo under "exact".
- The JLSF and Ningbo name-collision lists are incomplete.
- Minor squadron and position details are wrong.

Main omissions in the PLAN surface fleet: the Sovremenny destroyers (including hull Ningbo 139), Type 052B, 051C, 051B and 054. Also missing are the JH-7A maritime-strike aircraft, the PLARF conventional strike TELs (DF-21C, DF-15, DF-10A, CJ-10, CJ-100), the modern HQ-9 site, and a China-flagged SOSUS proxy.

inventory.method_notes:
Read-only; nothing in the repo was modified. Helper scripts are in (agent scratch, not kept) (index.py, nations.py, names.py, show.py).

Method:
(1) Enumerated every unit .ini under vessels/, aircraft/ and land_units/ in vanilla (mods-source/_vanilla/original), every mods-source/<id>, and every integration/*/SEST_* pack. Vanilla has no submarines/ folder; submarines live in vessels/. Each id was resolved with winning_file / find_unit_file / file_stack imported from integration/missions/refine_civ_traffic.py, giving 2133 winning units.
(2) Read the operator from Nation= and FlagTexture= in each winning _variants.ini / _squadrons.ini. Russia appears as Nation=Soviet; the winning nations_reference.ini (3416372890) has no Russia entry. Filtered on Nation=Soviet/RU and the wp_/ru_/rfn_ prefixes, then grepped ids, names and land units for every lens platform and node name (including Olenya, Engels, Ukrainka, Belaya, Severomorsk, Il-38N/Novella, Tu-22M3, Tu-142MZ, Ka-31, Lada/677, Elbrus/23120).
(3) Display names merged key by key across file_stack('language_en/<kind>_names.ini'), per docs/collection-interop-audit.md, which records that language files merge rather than override.
(4) For bases and ships, resolved every [AirGroup] aircraft id and recorded the misses. Parsed [SupplySystemN] blocks, ServiceDate windows, ReceiverSystems/TankerSystems and the AmmoPoints/SupplyCategory of key munitions.
(5) Checked vanilla campaign files for geolocated Russian anchors, and checked the repo missions for a Kola precedent (chapter 4 - Kill Kuznetsov).

Every unit id listed in mappings and installations was re-verified to resolve through find_unit_file. Winning sources marked SEST_Integration are integration/dist/SEST_Integration/<path>, which is built from integration/replenishment/SEST_Replenishment; the underlying Workshop owner is noted where file_stack shows one.

Hull-to-fleet allocations (Northern vs Pacific) are general knowledge, flagged as needing verification. They are not taken from the research reports, which were not available. Nothing is asserted about what R01-R03 say about these nodes.

corrections.problem: The note says the Nakhimov refit carries wp_ss-n-26 (9000, SovietAdvancedASM) and that Boris Chilikin can reload it. The winning file integration/dist/SEST_Integration/vessels/wp_rkr_admiral_nakhimov_refit.ini fires wp_ss_n_27 (8 launchers) and wp_ss_n_26a (8 launchers). Both come from mods-source/3413868677/ammunition and carry neither AmmoPoints nor SupplyCategory. wp_ss-n-26 (9000) is actually on wp_rkr_kirov_improved.
corrections.fix: Move the wp_ss-n-26 / Chilikin note to wp_rkr_kirov_improved. For the Nakhimov, say its Klub and Oniks are unpriced and uncategorised (integration/replenishment/README.md lines 320-325). Any Russian supplier in range can reload them free, including Kazbek, Pashin and the RE-power merchants. Only its wp_set-65 torpedoes (5220) need Chilikin or Don.

corrections.problem: The support evidence says 'The 200 cap blocks missile reloads'. That fails for the lens's coastal and SAM units, whose rounds are unpriced: Bastion wp_ss_n_26a, Bal wp_ss_n_25, the S-400 site's wp_40n6, wp_48n6e3, wp_9m96e and wp_9m96e2, and the 5P85TE2's wp_40h6e. MaxAmmoPoints has no price to compare against. The Bastion launcher also sets ReloadableWithoutMagazine=True.
corrections.fix: Say the Ural's 200 cap blocks only priced missiles. The one priced round on the lens SAM site is the wp_sa-n-6 (4950) launcher on wp_sam_site_sa-21. Bastion, Bal and the S-400 rounds can be trucked.

corrections.problem: Support evidence and the 'supply ships' mapping say the RE-power merchants can pass 'guns and point-defence SAMs only' and 'cannot pass ASMs or torpedoes'. civ_ms_kommunist, civ_ms_murom and civ_ms_slavyansk (3605013271) have no MaxAmmoPoints (so no cap) and no category lines, so every uncategorised round passes at any price. On surface ships that includes wp_set-65 and wp_53-65K torpedoes (5220/6600), wp_ss-n-16 (6450), wp_sa-n-6 / wp_sa-n-20 (4950), rfn_91r1 (3000), and unpriced Oniks/Klub (wp_ss_n_26a, wp_ss_n_27, rfn_3m55).
corrections.fix: Restate the limit: they block categorised rounds (SovietAdvancedASM, SEST_LandAttack, AirTorpedo) and all submarines (TargetTypes=Vessel). Everything uncategorised passes uncapped. Apply the same wording to civ_ms_murom and civ_ms_slavyansk.

corrections.problem: The support evidence says Pashin 'cannot pass Kalibr, Oniks or heavyweight torpedoes'. With a 2000 ceiling it does block rfn_3m14, rfn_3m54, rfn_3m22, wp_fizik-2 (4695) and wp_set-65 (5220). It still passes unpriced Oniks/Klub: rfn_3m55 on the rfn_ hulls, wp_ss_n_26a/wp_ss_n_27 on the rsa hulls and the Nakhimov, and wp_ss-n-26a/wp_ss-n-27a on Yasen and Akula. The same applies to wp_vt_kazbek.
corrections.fix: Change the text to 'cannot pass priced Kalibr/Zircon or heavyweight torpedoes; unpriced Oniks/Klub variants pass free'. Make the same change on wp_vt_kazbek.

corrections.problem: The note covers only the torpedo (wp_fizik-2 4695, Chilikin or Don). The Yasen's 8 VLS launchers (wp_ss-n-27a x4 from 3468260539, wp_ss-n-26a x4 from 3629144864) are unpriced, uncategorised and set ReloadableWithoutMagazine=True, so Kazbek and Pashin can reload them. wp_ssn_akula's wp_ss-n-27a is the same.
corrections.fix: Add that the cruise-missile tubes reload free from any Vessel+Submarine supplier. Only the torpedoes are gated to Chilikin or Don.

corrections.problem: The mapping says Chilikin is 'the only Russian supplier able to pass SovietAdvancedASM rounds below 13000 and heavyweight torpedoes'. wp_pb_don (8000, SovietAdvancedASM 12, AirTorpedo 30) does both. So do civ_ms_seabee Variant7/8, Soviet-flagged and SEST-patched (8000 ceiling, SovietAdvancedASM 8, SEST_LandAttack 16, Vessel+Submarine). The gap 'No Russian supplier can rearm Kalibr, Oniks or Zircon' is also wrong. Chilikin passes rfn_3m14 (4310), rfn_3m54 (4800) and rfn_3m22 Zircon (10000) through SEST_LandAttack, and Oniks is unpriced.
corrections.fix: Restate it: Chilikin is the only open-dated supplier for rounds of 8000-13000 points (wp_ss-n-26 9000, rfn_3m22 10000, wp_ss_n_14c 12000, SS-N-22 12300). Don (dated 1990-1998) and Seabee V7/V8 cover rounds of 8000 or less. Drop the Kalibr/Zircon gap.

corrections.problem: The winning variants file is mods-source/3455404959/vessels/wp_pb_don_variants.ini (load-order line 190), not vanilla or 3605013271. Variant8 there is Nation=Indonesia, flag_indonesia ('Ratulangi 400'). The end dates of 1990-1998 are correct.
corrections.fix: Record the variants source as 3455404959 and exclude Variant8 (Indonesian).

corrections.problem: The note says 'Vanilla variants end between 1991 and 2020'. In mods-source/_vanilla/original/vessels/wp_bpk_udaloy_variants.ini, Variant8 Severomorsk (1987), Variant9 Levchenko (1988) and Variant12 Panteleyev (1992) have no end date. The Default is 1980|1997.
corrections.fix: Say most vanilla variants are end-dated (1991-2020) but Severomorsk, Levchenko and Panteleyev are open-ended. wp_bpk_udaloy_98 remains the preferred choice.

corrections.problem: The inventory says it has no display name in any language_en file. mods-source/3411341227/language_en/aircraft_names.ini starts with a UTF-8 BOM before [wp_tu-95_bearg], which defeats a '^\[' grep. It defines Default='Tu-95K-22' and Squadron1-4 = 392nd ODRAP, 169th GAP, 304th ODRAP and 403rd OPLAP.
corrections.fix: Remove this item from gaps and the language-merging finding. The unit's display name is Tu-95K-22, a Cold War Kh-22 carrier, so it is not a modern Tu-95MS.

corrections.problem: The winning squadrons file mods-source/3438479626/aircraft/wp_ka-27_squadrons.ini declares Squadron9 and Squadron10 as Nation=Yuktobanian (a fictional Ace Combat nation). SEST_Integration language_en still names them 'Ka-27PL (85th PLAVP)' and '(8th PLAVP)', which look Russian. The placement finding says Erusea is the only non-Soviet value, which misses these.
corrections.fix: Use only Default and Squadron1-8 (Nation=Soviet). Flag Squadron9/10 as fictional-nation. The Kuznetsov's Squadron6 and the rfn hulls' Default are fine.

corrections.problem: The receiver list ('Only wp_mig-31bm, wp_tu-142m, wp_tu-22m2, wp_su_33 and wp_mig-29k') is incomplete. These Soviet-nation winners also declare ReceiverSystems=ProbeAndDrogue: wp_mig-29k_941, wp_mig-29k_947, wp_mig-29m_915, wp_mig-29m_961, wp_mig-29m2_967, wp_mig-29smt_918 (3417446309), wp_su-24m (vanilla), and wp_p_42_98, wp_taifun_98, wp_taifun_ew_98, wp_mig_23am_98, wp_su_47 (3413868677). The squadrons file also has an unnamed Squadron2 (comment 'VTA 708th').
corrections.fix: Expand the compatible-receiver list and note that only Squadron1 (203rd GARP) has a display name.

corrections.problem: The civil-traffic missing_fit rests on 'No modern Russian civil-flag texture appears anywhere in the collection'. Vanilla ui/Default/Settings_UI_General.ini [MastFlags] registers Russia=flag_rus,flag_civ_rus (line 126). The winning SEST_Integration copy adds Russia_Navy=flag_civ_rus and NationFlags Russia/Russia_Navy/RU=ui/bottom/flag_russia2.png. The repo's own 'chapter 4 - Kill Kuznetsov.ini' places civ_ms_*/civ_fv_okean with Nation=russia and warships with Nation=russia_navy (79 such lines across the chapter 2/3/4/6 missions). No unit file uses flag_rus or flag_civ_rus.
corrections.fix: Keep missing_fit for the unit-level FlagTexture, but say the fix is a mission Nation=russia / russia_navy key or a variant FlagTexture=flag_civ_rus, not a new texture. Revise the operator-key finding too: unit files use Nation=Soviet, while missions use russia / russia_navy.

verify.verdict:
Resolution is sound: all 79 unit IDs in mappings, installations and support_and_traffic resolve through find_unit_file / winning_file. The stated winning sources are correct, including the SEST_Integration-over-Workshop layering. The Kuznetsov, Kirov, Slava, Udaloy, Gorshkov, AirGroup, ServiceDate, capacity and non-resolving-AirGroup claims check out. The outcome labels (exact/proxy/missing_fit/none) are honest.

The main faults are in the rearm logic. The inventory ignores unpriced, uncategorised rounds: Red Storm Oniks and Klub, the Yasen and Akula Kalibr/Oniks, Bastion, Bal and the S-400 missiles. Supply ceilings cannot gate these, so the claims about Kazbek, Pashin, the merchants, the Ural truck and the Nakhimov are wrong.

There are also these factual errors:
- The Nakhimov carries wp_ss_n_27 and wp_ss_n_26a, not wp_ss-n-26.
- wp_tu-95_bearg is named Tu-95K-22; a BOM hid the name.
- Three vanilla Udaloy variants are open-ended.
- The Don variants come from 3455404959 and include an Indonesian Variant8.
- The Ka-27 Squadron9/10 are Yuktobanian.
- Russia mast flags (flag_rus, flag_civ_rus) are registered in vanilla, and the repo's missions use Nation=russia / russia_navy.

Missed assets: Sovremenny_98 and Tarantul III (resolving replacements for the stale Kola-mission IDs), Grisha V with Northern and Pacific hull names, Nanuchka III, Ropucha, and the Soviet-flag Seabee barge carriers (an open-dated supplier with an 8000 ceiling that serves submarines). Also missed: the nv_pt_boats_docks shore rearm proxy, S-300PMU/PS, S-350 and S-500 SAMs, Su-35S Pacific regiments, Tu-214R, the Pacific Tu-22M2 squadrons, Forpost-R, and RU-nation airliners.

gaps: Japan: no Kawasaki P-1 (Atsugi, Djibouti), Kongo DDG, Izumo/Kaga DDH, Akizuki/Murasame/Takanami DD, Abukuma DE, or Soryu/Taigei/Oyashio SSK. The only Japanese conventional submarines are Cold War vanilla classes. No Towada AOE, Osumi LST, MCH-101 or US-2. No named JMSDF or JASDF base: Atsugi, Kanoya, Naha and the Djibouti facility have only the generic airfield_small_1 Variant5.

Norway: no F-35A in Norwegian service (raaf_f-35a has only RAAF squadrons, and no USAF F-35A exists). No Fridtjof Nansen frigate, Ula submarine, Maud logistics ship or Norwegian NH90/SAR helicopter. No Evenes airbase. Modern Norwegian content is limited to the P-8A (usn_p8 Squadron5), Skjold corvettes, CB90 and the MMF MRTT.

Australia: no Hunter-class or any Type 26. Collins, Supply, Arafura and Choules exist only as SEST stand-in meshes. The HMAS Stirling port marker (ran_pt_boats_docks Variant2) has no supply or service function.

United Kingdom: no Chinook (CH-47 of any nation), Puma or modern SAR helicopter for Mount Pleasant. No UK F-35B squadron. No 1435 Flight Typhoon squadron. No HMS Protector or other ice/survey ship. No Queen Elizabeth carrier, Astute/Vanguard submarine, Albion LPD, Bay, Fort Victoria, Wave or Argus. No named Mount Pleasant, Mare Harbour or Akrotiri base. The only UK-flag airbase variant is 'RAF Gibraltar' on Iceland scenery.

France: no French replenishment ship (BRF Jacques Chevallier or Durance), Floréal surveillance frigate, Falcon 50M/2000 maritime aircraft, or SA330 Puma/AS555 Fennec for the Djibouti forces. No French base unit for Djibouti or Ile Longue. The Triomphant has no non-nuclear (M51-free) fit.

Italy: no Cavour, Trieste, San Giorgio, or Vulcano/Etna logistic ship, so the collection has no Italian supply ship at all. No P-72A at Sigonella; only the retired Br.1150 Atlantic exists. No Italian F-35A or F-35B. No Todaro Batch II. No named Italian base for Sigonella, Naples or Djibouti.
Spain: no Cantabria or Patiño AOR; the only Spanish supplier is the 1950s Teide oiler. No named Rota base unit.

Greece: no Hellenic Navy warship of any kind: Hydra/MEKO 200HN, Elli/Kortenaer, Kimon/FDI HN, Papanikolis/Type 214. No Greek naval helicopters (S-70B-6, AB-212). No Souda Bay base unit. The HAF F-16 340 and 343 Sqn liveries do exist.
Bahrain: no military unit is flagged Bahrain (no RBNS Sabha OHP, BDF F-16 or helicopters); only the Gulf Air civil liveries exist. There is no Muharraq or Bahrain naval support base unit.

UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Oman: no naval units for any of these states. UAE has no F-16E/F. Oman has only the Oman Air civil livery. No Jebel Ali port unit. The vanilla Gulf ports are hidden scenery, and three of them (Dammam, Fujairah, Minah al Ahmadi) wrongly declare Nation=Iceland.

Djibouti: no national forces, and no Djibouti nation key or flag. The collocated US, Chinese, French, Japanese and Italian facilities can only be marked with generic 'All'-flag installations (FOB, tents) or airbase clones.
Neutral traffic: no dhow or small-craft variant is flagged to a Gulf state, Oman or Djibouti.
inventory.method_notes:
Method and scope:

- **Resolution:** every unit ID was resolved with winning_file and find_unit_file, imported from integration/missions/refine_civ_traffic.py. Only SEST_Integration is in the load order (integration/dist/SEST_Integration); the per-pack SEST folders are consolidated into it.
- **Index:** I built a read-only index of all 2037 winning units under vessels/, aircraft/ and land_units/. For each unit it records UnitType, LandUnitSubType and HideIn from the unit file, and Nation per [VariantN] or [SquadronN] from the winning side file.
- **Display names:** language_en files merge key by key across the whole file stack, so names were merged from all copies. Reading only the winning copy misses names.
- **BOM handling:** files were read as UTF-8 with BOM handling. One mod's names file (3695809489, holding the Asahi name) starts with a BOM.
- **Discovery:** units were found by grepping Nation keys in the winning files, not by mod titles. Ids and display names were then checked for each lens platform; absence was confirmed by id and name searches.
- **Scratch files:** helper scripts and indexes are in (agent scratch, not kept)  (build_index.py, names_index.py, q.py, verify.py, index.json, names.json). No repository file was modified.
- **Research reports:** R01-R03 were not consulted, as instructed. Squadron-to-base pairings are lookups by squadron name and still need checking against the research.
- **Stand-in classification:** SEST stand-in clones whose name, operator and function match the platform are classed exact, with the stand-in mesh noted. Units from another operator or era are classed proxy.
- **Not tested:** whether the editor filters variants by ServiceDate, and how stand-ins behave in game.

corrections.problem: Wildcat is exact as an airframe, but it cannot embark on any of the RN escorts the inventory recommends. rn_ddg_type45, rn_ddg_type45_22 and rn_ddg_type45_26 (SEST_Integration) list AircraftSupported=...,rn_aw159, and rn_aw159 does not resolve: find_unit_file returns None. rn_ff_type23 and rn_ff_type23_mlu support only fr_as_532SC, rn_merlin_hm1/hm2 and rn_sea_lynx_mk8. The only hull that carries rn_wildcat is SEST_Integration:vessels/rn_type23_refit.ini, which uses a Knox mesh and variants from the deprecated 3378409795.

verify.verdict:
The inventory holds up on resolution. All 103 unit_ids resolve through find_unit_file and winning_file to the stated winning source. That covers 96 mapping IDs, 6 installation IDs and sp_a330_mrtt from support_and_traffic. Declared Nation keys, ServiceDates, supply and refuel blocks, the absence of a Djibouti nation key, hidden Gulf ports and Port placeability all check out. The confirmed 'none' gaps also stand: no P-1, Kongo, Nansen, Ula, Chinook, Type 26, Cantabria, Bahrain or Omani military unit, or Djibouti flag.

There are 14 corrections, mostly to notes rather than to IDs or outcomes. Three matter most:
- Embarked Wildcat does not work on the recommended Type 45 and Type 23 hulls. The Type 45s list the unresolved rn_aw159, and only the deprecated-variant rn_type23_refit carries rn_wildcat.
- The Type 212A chosen for the Ula and Greek stand-ins is the 2029-2037 upgraded version; the in-service unit is ger_ssk_type_212a_batch1.
- RAF Typhoon Squadron1 is 1(F) Sqn, not unnamed.

The other corrections:
- Yushio is not the only Japanese SSK.
- Dependencies on deprecated mods 3440622312 and 3403661005 are not flagged.
- The Greece warships entry should be split by class.
- The Stirling port marker should be missing_fit because it has no supply function.
- rn_type23 and rn_type23_refit win from SEST_Integration, not 3378409795.
- Minor display-name and date details: Skjold, Voyager, S80 Plus, Type 45 '26', and the Super Puma squadron pick.

The inventory missed several exact operator assets:
- **UK:** P-8 Poseidon MRA1, E-7 Wedgetail AEW.1 and RC-135W.
- **Australia:** the Canberra LHD and Choules, Super Hornet and Growler squadrons, extra named RAAF bases (Pearce, Learmonth, Curtin, Edinburgh) and RAAF P-8 squadrons in usn_p_8a.
- **Japan:** Patriot PAC-3, Type 12 SSM-ER and AH-64DJ.
- **France:** Charles de Gaulle with Rafale M and E-2D, Mistral, and the Gazelle for the Djibouti detachment.
- **Italy:** Durand de la Penne, Maestrale and SAMP/T.
- **Spain:** the Galerna SSK and Patriot.
- **Greece:** NH90, AH-64DN, Patriot and Velos.
- **Gulf:** Kuwait-flag merchants, which contradict the 'no Gulf-flagged traffic' gap.
- **Norway:** Norway-flag supply merchants.

Helper scripts are in (agent scratch, not kept) skeptic_allies/ (res.py, idx.py, idx.json, qn.py, nm.py, sup.py). No repository file was modified.

inventory.lens: installations, placement evidence, support and civilian traffic

mappings.notes: No named North Island unit. usa_airbase Variant1 is the generic 'Naval Air Station' (Nation=US), the best label without cloning. airbase_us is the template the raaf-bases builder clones. A named 'NAS North Island' clone with a CustomAirGroup follows that precedent. No repo mission has ever placed a unit near San Diego: the nearest proven sea point is 429 NM away and the nearest land point 3,298 NM. Validate the anchor with a coastline/land mask, because the proven-position snapper can't.
display_names: U.S. Air Force Base / Modern US Airbase (airbase_us)

mappings.notes: No named San Diego port. The vanilla world database has only a 'San Diego' city point (campaigns/us_cities_pacific.ini). nv_pt_boats_docks is the only generic naval-pier model the builders use. RE-power gives it effectively unlimited vessel rearm (AmmoCapacity 9,999,999,999, no ceiling, 3 nmi). Place it with Nation=usa only if unlimited shore rearm is intended; otherwise use warehouses or fuel tanks as non-supplying scenery.

No named base, no submarine tender and no working shipyard. nv_pt_boats_docks_small is RE-power's submarine-only pier with unlimited supply. US_Los_Alamos (USS Los Alamos AFDB-7 floating dock, subtype OilRig) is a target object with no repair function. The nearest proven sea placement is about 990 NM away.

Named vanilla Port 'Norfolk' (display 'Norfolk,Norflok' sic, Nation=US). HideIn=Encyclopedia,MissionEditor,Signatures, so it can't be picked in the editor. Vanilla places it via campaigns/us_ports_atlantic.ini (36.9226,-76.3429, Movements=5 civil destinations), which a mission can load in [BackgroundData] with LoadBackgroundData=True. No stock or repo mission loads that file. The unit has no SupplySystem. NAS Norfolk exists only as the airports.ini point KNGU, with no land unit. Nearest proven placements: sea 206 NM, land 1,689 NM.

Named vanilla ports (Nation=US). Mayport is Role=LargeMilitary in us_ports_atlantic.ini. Both are hidden from the editor and carry no supply. The aviation site (NAS Jacksonville) has no named unit; use the usa_airbase proxy.

mappings.role_family: naval air station (patrol, test and evaluation, training)
mappings.lookup_term: NAS Norfolk / NAS Jacksonville / Patuxent River / Whiting Field
mappings.notes: Generic NAS stand-in. Research, test and primary-training functions aren't modelled by any unit, so the role is flavour only. usa_airbase declares FlightDeck_AmmoCapacity 2,000,000. Its default air group is Cold War, so replace it with a mission CustomAirGroup.

mappings.lookup_term: Susquehanna, Richmond, San Joaquin, Anniston, Red River, Tobyhanna
mappings.notes: Only generic target buildings exist. tgt_ammo_depot_small has a finite LandUnit-only supply (200,000 points, 1.5 nmi), so it can't serve ships or aircraft. Distribution relationships aren't an engine mechanic; record them in the register. Anniston, Red River and Tobyhanna are hundreds of NM inland from any proven placement (Red River is 800 NM from proven sea). Tactical representation adds little.

No named unit. The vanilla airports.ini has Hickam (PHIK, LargeMilitary) and Kaneohe Bay (PHNG) as points only. The nearest proven sea placement is 1,159 NM away and the central Pacific has only 9 placed units in the whole corpus.

No named Apra unit. Stock 'All Your Guam Belong to Us' proved a land point at 13.30,144.70 (9 NM). nv_pt_boats_docks gives unlimited rearm; label it and decide whether that matches the finite-supply rule.

Stock vanilla 'Showdown off Guam Blue 1985' places airfield_small_1 Variant1 ('Airbase - small (USA)') at 13.59,144.94, 1 NM from Andersen, which is a proven anchor. Andersen also appears as vanilla airports.ini PGUA (LargeMilitary). nato_large_pvo_airbase1 holds B-52H x47 but is labelled 'Barksdale Air Force Base'. A named 'Andersen AFB' clone of airbase_us (raaf-bases method) is the clean route.
No named unit. Yokohama and Tokyo exist only as asia_ports.ini points (9 and 24 NM). The nearest proven land placement is 43 NM away (thaad_tel in the user mission 'GULF ATTACK .7.7').

No named PLAN base. Set Nation=china per placement. Stock PLAN 02 Battle of the South China Sea and pacific-strike-task-force '10 Vengeance at Luzon' proved land points 6-8 NM from Yulin and Longpo (airfield_small_1 at 18.29,109.43; wp_airbase_4 at 18.30,109.72). Both piers carry RE-power unlimited supply.

No vessel file carries a fuel key; ship fuel isn't modelled in the data. UnlimitedFuel is documented (language_en/ui.ini UnlimitedFuelTooltip) for aircraft and helicopters. 'Oiler' suppliers transfer only ammunition points. Air-to-air refuelling (RefuelSystem) exists for aircraft only.

AmmoCapacity is a finite stock that depletes and 'does not refill at sea' (docs/replenishment-in-play.md). Suppliers can top up each other's own weapons but not each other's supply pools. No port restocks a supplier. RE-power records that AmmoCapacity=Unlimited does not work.

gaps: No named installation unit exists for most plan nodes: Coronado/North Island, San Diego, Kitsap/Puget Sound, Patuxent River, Whiting Field, all six DLA/Army depots, San Joaquin, Pearl Harbor, Guam/Apra, Andersen, Yokosuka, Yulin, Longpo, Lingshui, Ningbo, the six JLSF centres, Ukrainka, Belaya, Kanoya, Atsugi, Naha, Evenes, Diego Garcia, Bahrain/NSA, Muharraq, Jebel Ali, every Djibouti facility, Rota, Naples, Sigonella, Souda Bay, Akrotiri, Germersheim, Mount Pleasant, Mare Harbour and Ile Longue. Only Norfolk, Jacksonville/Mayport, Severomorsk/Kola (port, fuel depot, warehouses, Gremikha), Olenya, Engels, HMAS Stirling and RAAF Tindal have named units.

The named vanilla US East Coast and Soviet ports are hidden from the mission editor (HideIn) and carry no supply. They reach a mission only through [BackgroundData] world-database files, which is untested for a sandbox.
No Aegis Ashore, SPY-1, SM-3 or land Mk41 unit for Deveselu or Redzikowo. THAAD and AN/TPY-2 or Patriot are different systems.

No Djibouti nation flag, so the host nation can't be shown. No UK-, France-, Italy- or Norway-flagged airbase variant (only 'RAF Gibraltar' variants for the UK); per-placement Nation overrides are needed.

Data quirks in winning files: port_pg_dammam, port_pg_fujairah and port_pg_minah_al_ahmadi have Nation=Iceland (vanilla); airbase_us Variant2 'Rammstein' has Nation=Germany; civ_ms_sealift_pacific has no display name; FOB (3600788156) has no display name.

No submarine tender (except the Cold War Soviet Don), no shipyard or drydock function (US_Los_Alamos is a target object), and no repair at sea or in port outside Task Force Mode between-mission flags.
Ship fuel isn't modelled: no vessel fuel keys. 'Oilers' pass ammunition only. Fuel transfer exists only as air-to-air refuelling for aircraft.

No finite shore-side vessel supply. The only shore suppliers are RE-power's nv_pt_boats_docks and nv_pt_boats_docks_small (effectively unlimited, no ceiling). All 39 vanilla port units and the RADF docks have none.

Supplier pools can't be restocked: AmmoCapacity depletes and doesn't refill at sea, and no port restocks a supplier. Carrier air wings can't be rearmed at sea, since no supplier tops up FlightDeck_ magazines.

Modern airbases (airbase_us and all 17 SEST RAAF/RNZAF clones, wp_airbase_modern, pla_airbase_modern, plaaf_airlift_airbase, wp_tu160air, wp_airbase_57, airfield_us/_large/_wp/_a-10, se_airbase_JAS_39) declare no FlightDeck_AmmoCapacity, so their aircraft-ordnance stock is the undocumented engine default.

No French, Italian, Norwegian, Indian or modern Spanish replenishment ship. ran_oa_supply and idn_vt_uda are Role=RAS but have no supply block. The JMSDF has only the Mashuu stand-in (no Towada) and the RFA only the Tide stand-in (no Fort Victoria or Wave). The PLAN, JMSDF, RFA, RAN and modern USN suppliers are SEST stand-ins on donor meshes.

RE-power's 14 merchant hulls (civ_ms_freighter_a/b/d, poltava, amra, andizhan, irkutsk, kommunist, murom, slavyansk, metallurg_anosov, super_p, yuniy_partizan, wp_ms_andizhan_armed) carry live supply blocks: 2.4-12 million points, no ceiling, near-instant transfer. Used as 'neutral traffic' they are latent unlimited suppliers; behaviour when neutral is untested.

Civilian shipping gaps: no LNG carrier, no modern large container ship (all boxships are 1970s-80s), no ferry or ro-pax, no cruise ship (only the Soviet Ivan Franko liner), no yachts, and no product tanker except the US MSC T-AOT.

Flag gaps for neutral merchants and fishing boats: no China, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Bahrain, UAE, Saudi, Oman, Yemen, Somalia, Djibouti, Marshall Islands or Bahamas variants (Kuwait, Panama, Liberia, Malta, Cyprus and Singapore exist). No Chinese fishing fleet, maritime militia or China Coast Guard hull; civ_fv_sampan is Vietnam-only.
No Western or Chinese civil cargo aircraft (civ_il-76t/td are Soviet-flag only; civ_il-18 cargo is Mali). No Boeing airliners; the modern airliners are Airbus A320/A330/A380 only.

The US domestic nodes (San Diego, Kitsap, Norfolk, Jacksonville, Pearl Harbor and the inland depots) have essentially no proven placement points (20 placed units on the US east coast, 10 on the Americas' Pacific coast, 9 around Hawaii and the central Pacific). The only committed coastline extract covers [100,-72,180,-25], so they need new land/sea validation.

Inland nodes (Anniston, Red River, Tobyhanna, Susquehanna, Germersheim, Engels, Belaya, Ukrainka, Xining, Zhengzhou, Wuhan, Guilin, Shenyang) are hundreds to more than 1,100 NM from any placed unit; terrain behaviour there is untested.
No measured active-unit, performance or save/reload limits exist in the repo. The largest loaded saves are about 974 entries (Indo-Pacific Land Assets) and 536 units (Banda Front Lean v2).
inventory.method_notes: Read-only. Resolution used integration/missions/refine_civ_traffic.py winning_file/find_unit_file (load order from data/load-order.tokens.txt: SEST_Integration -> integration/dist/SEST_Integration, then 197 workshop ids, unlisted mods, then vanilla), imported via sys.path. Unit enumeration: the union of every vessels/, aircraft/ and land_units/ *.ini basename across vanilla, all mods-source/<id> and integration/*/SEST_* packs (excluding _variants/_squadrons/_loadouts), each resolved through winning_file, with LandUnitSubType read from the winning file. Totals: Airbase 55, Port 48, Installation 36, plus MobileUnit 141, SAM 107, Radar 56, MissileSite 23, AAA 15, OilRig 3, Bridge 3. Installations lists all 139 Airbase/Port/Installation winners plus four related units (US_Los_Alamos, civ_spar_rig, civ_spar_rig_helo, thaad_tel). Nation is the 'Nation=' key in the winning <unit>_variants.ini (per [Default]/[VariantN]) for ships and land units, and per [SquadronN] in the winning <unit>_squadrons.ini for aircraft. Missions can override it per unit with 'Nation='. Display names come from merging every language_en/*names*.ini section across sources in load-order priority (highest wins). Supply data are the [SupplySystemN] keys of the winning file (all SEST supplier hulls resolve to SEST_Integration). Placement statistics: every mission *.ini with MapCenterLatitude under integration/missions, integration/campaign/SEST_Campaign, integration/dist/SEST_Integration, mods-source/_vanilla/original/{missions,campaigns/*/missions}, mods-source/_vanilla/user/missions and mods-source/*/missions or campaigns/*/missions (842 files; 608 after dropping 'backup', '_temp' and 'user_missions_dev' copies). Absolute positions use lat=c+z/60, lon=c+x/60, with x wrapped to ±180 for the distance tables. Node coordinates used to measure distances are approximate public locations I supplied (e.g. Andersen 13.58,144.93; Olenya 68.15,33.46), not research-report data. Distances are flat-earth NM and only indicative. I didn't read the R01-R03 research reports and assert nothing about what they say about nodes. Helper scripts live only in the session scratchpad ((agent scratch, not kept) spenum.py, land.py, landall.py, supply.py, civ.py, missions.py, nodes.py, inst.py, sup.py, maps.py, final.py; the full payload is in final.json there). Nothing in the repo was modified. Not verified in game: HideIn placement via BackgroundData, per-unit Nation flag rendering, neutral-supplier behaviour, airbase default ordnance stock, and terrain at unplaced nodes.

placement_and_engine.finding: RelativePositionInNM is x,alt,z in plain arcminutes on both axes, not true nautical miles in x: lat = MapCenterLatitude + z/60 and lon = MapCenterLongitude + x/60, with no cos(lat) scaling. The alt field may be a number or a band word such as 'low' on land units. Waypoints use the same frame.
placement_and_engine.evidence: integration/campaign/build_pack.py harvest() docstring: 'RelativePositionInNM is plain arcminutes on both axes. Checked against the two RAAF bases NORTHERN FRONT II places - Darwin resolves to -12.427,130.884 and Scherger to -12.603,142.040, both within a mile'. Writers emit (lon-c)*60,(lat-c)*60 (build_pack.py about line 1594; build_indo_pacific_showcase.py line 391). Cross-check: stock 'Strawberries Can Kill' Blue (centre 42.27,168.58) and Red (centre 54.27,-26.28, x=12117.71) both resolve to the same NW Pacific area only under the plain-arcminute rule; cos-scaling would put the Red carrier in the mid-Atlantic.

placement_and_engine.finding: There are 192 distinct map centres in 608 non-backup mission files across integration/missions, integration/campaign (SEST_Campaign), dist/SEST_Integration, vanilla stock missions and campaigns, vanilla user exports and 17 mods' missions. The most common is the editor default (54.27,-26.28) in 92 files, including 3 stock vanilla missions and every Northern Front/AUS DEF save. Next come Banda (-6.0,130.0) x38, Bab-el-Mandeb (13.17,43.15) x19 in the Black Widow/YF-23 mod 3796349767, and Southern Watch (-10.0,131.0) x8. Kola (69.25,33.23) x7, Hormuz (25.78,55.74) x6, the Gulf (25.87,53.73) x6, the US west coast offshore (30.0,-125.0) x6 and the US east coast (34.0,-74.0) x4 also recur. SEST campaigns centre between -60.0,118.0 and 9.75,116.1. Other mods add the Falklands (-54.27,-36.44), Mozambique Channel (-11.82,42.95), Grenada (12.02,-61.76), the Gulf of Finland (60.02,29.75) and the Antarctic (-76.54,127.45, chapter 5 Polar Pickup).
placement_and_engine.evidence: Scan of every *.ini with MapCenterLatitude (scratch script missions.py). Examples: integration/missions/chapter 4 - Kill Kuznetsov.ini (69.25,33.23); mods-source/_vanilla/original/missions/NATO/Hormuz.ini (25.78,55.74); mods-source/3796349767/missions/Black Widow - Southern Watch/03 Glass Needle.ini (13.17,43.15); integration/missions/chapter 5 - Polar Pickup.ini (-76.54,127.45).

placement_and_engine.finding: Very large offsets load and save. Largest found: 21,549 NM (x=21,519-21,549, centre 29.18,-179.92, EUROMOD showcase german). placement_and_engine.finding: (1) The campaign builder snaps to proven positions. harvest() pools every lat/lon a loading mission put a vessel, submarine or biologic (sea) or land unit (land) on, from integration/missions, vanilla missions, vanilla campaigns and vanilla user missions. Snapper.take() hands out the nearest unused point within 60 NM, or stops the build. open_water() uses an authored offshore point exactly if it is more than 25 NM (OPEN_SEA) from all land points, snaps it within 8 NM (OFFSHORE_SNAP) of a proven sea point, or refuses it. coastal=True gives a per-unit snap. (2) CoastPlacer and coast.py use tools/make_coast_extract.py: Natural Earth 1:10m land clipped to a box. The only committed extract is integration/campaign/geo/southern_theatre_coast.json, box [100,-72,180,-25] with 111 rings; it checks on_land and nm_to_coast and requires 2 NM of water for offshore stations. Another theatre needs a new extract (--box W S E N --name). (3) Mission tools use the global-land-mask 1 km mask: fix_land_positions.py (spiral search in 0.05 degree steps up to about 120 NM), sea_routes.py (A* on a 0.025 degree grid with lane caching), thin_waypoints.py and trim_land_sites.py re-check legs. (4) tools/preflight.py checks unit, variant, squadron and loadout references only, not positions. For the US home nodes, the Norway and Mediterranean nodes and Djibouti, the snapper finds no proof, so a new coast extract or the land mask is needed.

Entries in campaigns/*_ports.ini and *_installations.ini carry LandUnit=, Location=lat,lon, Nation, Role and Heading, and civil ports also carry Movements= and Destinations={Port X,1,civ_} links. A mission pulls them in with [Environment] LoadBackgroundData=True and a [BackgroundData] block (NumberOfBackgroundPortFiles, BackgroundPortFile1_Path=\campaigns\<file>.ini, likewise for Airport, Installation and City files). Only Operation Morvarid references persian_gulf_ports.ini, as a BackgroundAirportFile with LoadBackgroundData=False. placement_and_engine.finding: No unit cap, frame-rate budget or memory limit is documented anywhere in the repo. The largest files that the game loaded and re-exported: SEST Indo-Pacific Land Assets has 974 Type= entries (63 sites, 959 land units; the README calls it 'a clean sandbox save'). SEST Banda Front has 857 (794 land units). Banda Front Lean v2 has 536 units, 396 on land, 51 civil ships and 37 civil aircraft, and was edited in the game on 20 Sep. NORTHERN FRONT III FINAL NEWEST has 269. The trims (trim_land_sites.py, thin_waypoints.py) were justified by map clutter and editing convenience, not performance. The mod catalog flags one load-time issue ('Long carrier load time', Air Deck Operations Nimitz). The world-sandbox docs require measuring active-unit scope, time compression and save/reload rather than assuming them.

placement_and_engine.topic: Editor round-trip hazards for a persistent world
placement_and_engine.finding: Re-saving in the editor rewrites the file. Measured on Lean v2: every WeaponStatus=Hold or Tight came back Free; formation followers lost their Waypoints; CustomAirGroup=True lines with no aircraft were dropped. Neutral airfields whose files carry an [AirGroup] (airfield_small_1's default group spawns F-4s, an E-3A and P-3Cs) launch aircraft unless they get an explicitly empty CustomAirGroup=True. A unit with no Waypoints orbits its spawn, so civil aircraft need airways. restore_roe.py and extend_civil_airways.py exist for these.
placement_and_engine.evidence: docs/design-notes.md 'What an editor round-trip keeps' (lines 103-140); integration/missions/trim_land_sites.py docstring (neutral airfields grounded); integration/campaign/build_pack.py comment about civil aircraft orbiting (about line 1597).

placement_and_engine.finding: [CivilianRouteN] sections spawn units repeatedly. Stock Hormuz: SpawnFrom and DespawnAt a land unit, StartTime, SpawnInterval=min,max, MaxUnits, SpawnInGroupsOf, AllowedUnits, AllowedNations, AllowedLoadouts and relative Waypoints; the changelog calls this the Air Operations tab for legacy CivilianRoutes. Waypoints support Loop=True (30 uses). vanilla patrol_areas.ini defines Fishing, MaritimePatrol, ContinuousDeterrent and Espionage areas. A respawning CivilianRoute conflicts with the plan's finite-allocation rule unless MaxUnits is bounded and losses are accounted for. No SEST mission uses CivilianRoutes; SEST builders author explicit civil waypoints instead.

placement_and_engine.finding: integration/raaf-bases/build_pack.py: (1) TEMPLATE = mods-source/3592460366/land_units/airbase_us.ini (Modern US Airbase, which reuses vanilla Reykjavik airbase scenery and flight-deck geometry). (2) For each base id it regex-replaces the block from [AirGroup] to [FlightDeck] with a commented description and 'aircraft_id=SquadronN,count|SquadronM,count' lines, and sets DisplayClassName. (3) It writes <id>_variants.ini: AllVariantsAreOfSameNation=true, NumberOfVariants=1, Default/Variant1 Nation=<key> (the game's own key, e.g. NewZealand with no space). (4) It writes language_en/land_units_names.ini entries [<id>] Type=Airbase, Default=<name>, Variant1=<name>,Airbase. (5) Before writing anything it validates that every aircraft id exists in the SEST packs, workshop mods or vanilla, and that every squadron index is at most the count of [SquadronN] sections actually defined (not NumberOfSquadrons; the F-22 mod declares 7 and defines 1), failing the build otherwise. (6) It writes _info.ini. tools/build_all.py consolidates the output into SEST_Integration, which must stay first in load order (check_load_order.py). Result: 17 bases, 268 aircraft, capacity 200 each, one shared scenery model, no coordinates (each mission places the base), and no FlightDeck_AmmoCapacity, so finite ordnance must be added by a per-mission FlightDeck_ override or in the clone. The same clone-donor-to-new-id pattern is used for vessels by integration/ran-fleet and integration/replenishment (CLONES), and could carry named ports by cloning a dock or port model without HideIn (untested).

corrections.problem: The mapping display name '(no display name)' and the gaps data-quirk entry are wrong. language_* files merge key by key (docs/interoperability-report.md, integration/name-fixes/build_patch.py docstring). 3406985435's empty [civ_ms_sealift_pacific] section adds no keys, so the lower-priority 3432592449 keys still apply: Type 'MS,Tanker', Default 'Medium Tanker,Merchant', Variant1 'MV Sealift Pacific Ocean T-AOT-168', and so on. The inventory merged names section by section, which caused this.
corrections.fix: Set the display name to 'Medium Tanker,Merchant' (3432592449: language_en/vessel_names.ini) and drop it from the gaps data-quirk list. Re-derive all display names with a key-level merge.

corrections.problem: The installations list them with empty display names, and the gaps say 'FOB (3600788156) has no display name'. With a key-level merge, 3600788156 language_en/land_units_names.ini supplies Default 'Forward Operating Base,FOB', 'Omega Trench,U Trench' and 'T Bunker Trench,Bunker T'. SEST_Integration adds only the Variant1 'Desert' names.
corrections.fix: Fill in the display names and remove the FOB 'no display name' quirk from the gaps.

corrections.problem: The display name 'Airfield small' is the unit file's DisplayClassName. The language name is 'Field Drone Squad, Field Drone Squad' (3601891050: language_en/land_units_names.ini). That file starts with a UTF-8 BOM, so a naive parser misses its first section.
corrections.fix: Set the display name to 'Field Drone Squad'.

corrections.problem: The 'exact' outcome for a US Navy naval base is overstated. The unit is the named city port, and its only placement route (vanilla campaigns/us_ports_atlantic.ini [Port Norfolk]) declares Role=Civil with Movements=5 civil destinations. Its location, 36.9226,-76.3429, is the commercial terminal about 2 NM south of the Naval Station piers. Nothing in the data marks it as the naval station.
corrections.fix: Downgrade to proxy: a named commercial port standing in for Naval Station Norfolk. State Role=Civil, no supply, hidden from the editor.

corrections.problem: It is labelled 'exact' for a US Navy naval station, but us_ports_atlantic.ini [Port Jacksonville] declares Role=Civil. Only [Mayport] is Role=LargeMilitary.
corrections.fix: Keep port_eastcoast_mayport as exact (NS Mayport). Mark port_eastcoast_jacksonville as proxy (civil port).

corrections.problem: It sits inside the 'exact' Severomorsk main-fleet-base mapping. Variant1 'Gremikha PVO Airbase' is an air-defence interceptor base about 145 NM east of Severomorsk, not part of the Northern Fleet base.
corrections.fix: List it as related/proxy (Kola air defence) rather than as an exact element of the Severomorsk fleet base.

verify.verdict:
The inventory resolves correctly, but it needs revisions before use. I re-resolved all 240 unique unit IDs (388 claims across mappings, installations and support_and_traffic) with refine_civ_traffic.winning_file/find_unit_file. Every claimed winning source matches the actual winning file. The other checks also hold:
- Nation keys match the winning variants and squadrons files.
- Supply pools, ceilings and ranges match.
- FlightDeck_AmmoCapacity and AircraftCapacity values match.
- HideIn flags match.
- The listed AirGroup contents match.
- All 139 Airbase, Port and Installation winners are covered.
- No Aegis Ashore, SM-3 or SPY-1 land unit exists.
- No China or GCC merchant flag exists other than Kuwait.

Problems, by area:
- **Display names:** they were merged section by section instead of key by key. As a result civ_ms_sealift_pacific, FOB, Omega_trench and TBunkerTrench show as having no name, and dronesquad705_1 shows the wrong name.
- **Outcome labels:** several "exact" labels are overstated.
  - The Norfolk and Jacksonville ports are Role=Civil world-database ports.
  - Gremikha (wp_large_pvo_airbase) is not part of the Severomorsk fleet base.
  - wp_tu160air is not named Engels.
  - Nine SEST supplier clones are labelled stand-ins on donor meshes.
- **Air groups:** wp_airbase_modern has 10 of 61 aircraft that don't resolve, so there is no Tu-22M3 or Tu-95MS-X101. pla_airbase_modern has 7 of 56 unresolved, so it has no H-6 at all. The inventory also wrongly dismisses the generic Default variants of both bases.
- **Placement details:** several are misattributed.
  - The RAN dock at Fremantle is ran_pt_boats_docks_small.
  - The Falklands placements are from The Royal Navy mod, and the airbase is at Goose Green, not Stanley.
  - The Souda placement is Greek-flagged.
  - The Kanoya and Atsugi distances are conflated.
- **Missed assets:**
  - the C-141B's PlaneCargoSupplySystem, the only air ammunition-cargo system;
  - nato_ewr_station's UK, French, Spanish, Greek and Australian variants;
  - Second Northern War missions as a working precedent for loading the Severomorsk world-database files;
  - several host-nation tankers.
